title: How was Brasília built so fast?
hook: A whole capital, raised on the Cerrado in little more than three years.
summary: Under Juscelino Kubitschek, thousands of workers called candangos built Brasília in about 41 months; it opened on 21 April 1960.

cardBlocks.text: Campaigning in 1955, Juscelino Kubitschek promised to follow the Constitution and move the capital inland. Once elected, he made Brasília part of a development plan that promised "fifty years in five". The work fell to thousands of laborers from many regions of Brazil, above all the Northeast: the candangos.

The pace set a record. Construction took about 41 months, from 1956 to the inauguration on 21 April 1960, a date chosen to honour Tiradentes, a hero of Brazil’s fight against colonial rule. Many candangos refused to leave the city they had built from scratch, and stayed.
With thousands of candangos, Brasília was built in about 41 months and opened on 21 April 1960.

deepDiveBlocks.text: It depends where you start counting. From the start of work in 1956 to the inauguration was about 41 months. From the "stake zero", driven into the ground on 20 April 1957, it was three years.

The candangos came from many parts of Brazil, and many arrived fleeing the Great Drought of 1958 in the Northeast. Women worked on it too: IBGE’s experimental census of 1959 counted 2,966 economically active women in Brasília. The first laborers slept in sheds; in December 1956, the Free City appeared, today the Núcleo Bandeirante district.
The city was inaugurated at midnight on 21 April, during an open-air Mass on the Square of the Three Powers. The celebrations lasted three days, until the night of 23 April.

heroMedia.alt: Diagram of Brasília being built: trucks bring in candangos, cranes raise the Congress towers among scaffolding, and a bar of months shows the work nearly finished.
